item.title: Re: How do you pronounce the word 'keter'?
item.content:encoded:
Fair enough.

Kabbalah definitely does exist in the SCP universe on reflection—the entire Fifth Church and by extension the Antimemetics canon are based on an incoherent "religion" that draws on the "Fifth World", or adam kadmon, a Kabbalistic concept of the primordial and divine light that preceded and takes precedence over the "four worlds" of creation and represents the universe's true essence. In particular this has resonance with SCP-3125 which is basically the "divine light" restoring mankind to its pure and primordial state, except seen from a perspective where that primordial state is in fact evil.

The idea of the Foundation existing in a world where God is evil and humanity revolted against Him would also explain why "Keter" is used for the anomalies that are the most inimical and dangerous to human life, whereas the kabbalistic term refers to the unity, perfection and unknowability of God ("I am that I am").

item.title: Re: How do you pronounce the word 'keter'?
item.content:encoded: For "thawmeel", it's for sake of a joke SCP :) .

item.title: Re: How do you pronounce the word 'keter'?
item.content:encoded:
I was extremely surprised the first time I listened to a scp related podcast and heard someone say "keeter" and "thawmeel" (and initially had no idea what they were saying) but in retrospect it makes sense that most people here don't speak Hebrew and therefore wouldn't know. There is, at least in theory, a "correct" pronunciation which would be used in-universe, because most Foundation employees would presumably encounter the term via employee orientations and in-person job training etc, and the lack of a settled pronunciation here is just a result of the SCP Wiki being a text-only format.

(keh-ter; tah-u-mee-el; both words are accented on the final syllable at least in Modern Hebrew. Of course the "th" in "Thaumiel" is the Hebrew letter ת which does vary in pronunciation between dialects.)

Of course there is a surprising lack of kabbalistic/gematric anomalies here despite the large number based on the Old Testament, so this does presume that kabbalah exists in the SCP universe (to be fair, there is SCP-1313 which implies that knowing the numerological value of a bear allows you to summon one, which has a lot in common with gematria, but it's not explicitly part of the article). If it doesn't, I guess you could say "oh, it's named after Dr. Jim Keter, who invented the 5m x 5m x 5m containment chamber, and is pronounced kee-ter" or whatever

item.title: Re: How do you pronounce the word 'keter'?
item.content:encoded: KEH-ter. The accent is on the first syllable, and both e's are pronounced like the e in "met," and you draw out the vowel sounds a little longer than you would in English. It doesn't get the "ur" ending that "sweater" has for most English speakers. I've been speaking Hebrew since kindergarten. It's finally useful.
